patents.title: Soil-moisture irrigation that only waters when needed
patents.original_idea: A soil probe next to each sprinkler blocks watering when the soil is already moist.
patents.why_it_stalled: Sensors, valves and controllers were costly and needed mains power and wiring, so it suited golf courses and rich farms only.
patents.what_changed: Capacitive soil sensors cost about ₹150–300, a microcontroller with Wi-Fi/GSM about ₹300, and solar pumps are subsidised in India (PM-KUSUM).
patents.product_idea: A solar-powered soil-moisture controller that switches a farm pump on and off and sends SMS/WhatsApp alerts in local languages. Sold to farmers, or bundled with solar pump installers.
patents.who_it_helps: Smallholder farmers (India has ~100 million farm households); saves water, diesel/electricity and labour of night-time pump runs.
patents.build_cost: Prototype roughly ₹3,000–6,000; unit cost at scale perhaps ₹2,000–4,000.
patents.risks: Several Indian agri-tech startups already sell similar devices — needs a clear price or simplicity edge. Sensor durability in salty soil.

patents.title: Phone camera reads urine test strips for pregnancy & kidney checks
patents.original_title: Toilet device with system for inspecting health conditions
patents.original_idea: A toilet that dips a test strip in urine and reads it automatically to report health conditions.
patents.why_it_stalled: Needed a costly built-in analyser and display inside a special toilet.
patents.what_changed: Any smartphone camera plus colour-correction software can now read a standard ₹10–20 dipstick accurately.
patents.product_idea: An app for community health workers (ASHA workers) that reads urine strips with a phone camera to flag protein (pre-eclampsia risk), glucose and infection in pregnant women, and logs results.
patents.who_it_helps: Pregnant women in villages without labs; pre-eclampsia is a major cause of maternal deaths.
patents.build_cost: App prototype mostly software: ₹0–20,000 if you build it yourself; colour-calibration card printing is cheap.
patents.risks: A medical-device approval (CDSCO) is likely needed for diagnosis claims. Competitors exist abroad (e.g. Healthy.io), so local language + offline use is the edge.

patents.title: Low-cost suction dressing for diabetic foot wounds
patents.original_idea: Healing wounds faster by sealing them with foam and a cover and applying gentle vacuum.
patents.why_it_stalled: Not a failure — it became a big business — but the pumps and dressings stayed very expensive, so poor patients rarely get it.
patents.what_changed: Tiny battery micro-pumps cost a few hundred rupees; even simple mechanical (spring/bellows) vacuum versions have been shown to work in research.
patents.product_idea: A cheap, reusable negative-pressure pump with low-cost foam dressings for district hospitals and home care, especially diabetic foot ulcers that lead to amputations.
patents.who_it_helps: Diabetic patients at risk of amputation (India has ~100 million diabetics), burn and trauma patients.
patents.build_cost: Prototype ₹5,000–15,000; must then fund clinical testing.
patents.risks: Medical device regulation and clinical trials take time and money; needs a doctor/hospital partner. Check for newer patents on specific pump designs.

patents.title: Health-worker kit: BP, sugar and oxygen readings sent to a doctor
patents.original_idea: Turning a video-game console into a health monitor: plug in a glucose meter, show results on a TV, send them to a clinic by phone line.
patents.why_it_stalled: Needed a special console, cartridges and landlines; very few homes had them.
patents.what_changed: Every health worker has an Android phone; Bluetooth BP cuffs, oximeters and glucometers are cheap; India has the free eSanjeevani teleconsultation network.
patents.product_idea: A low-cost kit + offline app for ASHA workers that records readings from Bluetooth devices and shares a summary with a doctor, focused on high BP and diabetes.
patents.who_it_helps: Rural patients with chronic disease who rarely see a doctor.
patents.risks: Government and NGO apps exist; selling to government is slow. Data privacy rules (DPDP Act).

patents.title: Rent-a-solar cart for street vendors
patents.original_idea: A solar generator on wheels: battery box, folding solar panel on a mast, and a power panel.
patents.why_it_stalled: Lead-acid batteries were heavy and short-lived; solar panels were expensive.
patents.what_changed: Solar panels are now ~₹25–30 per watt and lithium-iron-phosphate batteries last 3,000+ cycles and weigh a third as much.
patents.product_idea: A pushable solar cart with LED lights, phone charging and a fan/blender socket, rented daily to street-food and night-market vendors who now use kerosene or diesel gensets.
patents.who_it_helps: Street vendors (India has ~10 million), saving fuel costs and fumes.
patents.build_cost: Prototype about ₹15,000–25,000 (200 W panel, 1 kWh LiFePO4, inverter, cart).
patents.risks: Battery theft and damage; collecting daily rent; existing solar-lantern businesses.

patents.title: Solar capacitive deionization for salty or fluoride groundwater
patents.original_title: Method and apparatus for capacitive deionization and electrochemical purification and regeneration of electrodes
patents.original_idea: Removing salt from water by passing it between charged carbon electrodes that hold the ions, then releasing them to regenerate.
patents.why_it_stalled: Good carbon electrodes were expensive and power electronics were costly.
patents.what_changed: Activated-carbon cloth and graphite sheets are cheap; solar power and simple controllers make it run off-grid. It wastes far less water than RO.
patents.product_idea: A village or school water unit for brackish or fluoride-contaminated groundwater (Rajasthan, Telangana, Gujarat), powered by solar, sold to panchayats or NGOs.
patents.who_it_helps: Tens of millions of Indians drink fluoride or high-salinity water.
patents.risks: Performance with real groundwater needs testing; RO is the established competitor; maintenance in villages.

patents.title: Prefab smart biogas unit for 2–5 cow households
patents.original_idea: A simple, single-tank digester that turns manure into methane with little skill or supervision.
patents.why_it_stalled: Farm-scale digesters were bulky, needed construction and frequently failed without anyone noticing.
patents.what_changed: Prefabricated HDPE/PVC digesters, cheap gas-pressure and temperature sensors, and phone alerts can catch problems early.
patents.product_idea: A factory-made biogas kit for small dairy households, with a sensor that messages the owner and installer when gas output drops, plus a slurry-as-fertiliser buy-back.
patents.who_it_helps: Rural women who cook on wood or dung fires (smoke is a major cause of illness).
patents.build_cost: Prototype ₹20,000–40,000; government biogas subsidies may apply.
patents.risks: Many past biogas units were abandoned due to poor maintenance — the service model matters more than the hardware. Existing makers (e.g. Sistema.bio).

patents.title: Phase-change carrier for vaccines and insulin
patents.original_title: Portable apparatus for storing and/or transporting biological samples, tissues and/or organs
patents.original_idea: A transport box that uses a phase-change material plus a cold core to hold a steady low temperature.
patents.why_it_stalled: Phase-change materials and good insulation were pricey; there was no cheap way to prove temperature was kept.
patents.what_changed: Phase-change materials at fixed temperatures are widely available, and a ₹300 Bluetooth temperature logger can prove the cold chain.
patents.product_idea: A carrier that holds 2–8 °C for days without electricity, with a temperature logger readable by phone, for insulin users and village vaccination drives.
patents.who_it_helps: Insulin users without reliable fridges; health workers carrying vaccines.
patents.risks: Must be tested to WHO-type standards for vaccines; insulin home use is an easier first market.

patents.title: Solar cold room for farmer groups, pay-per-crate
patents.original_idea: A foldable refrigerated room that ships like a shipping container and works without a foundation.
patents.why_it_stalled: Refrigeration needed grid power or diesel, so it suited emergency or military use only.
patents.what_changed: Cheap solar, efficient inverter compressors and "ice battery" thermal storage let a cold room run off-grid overnight.
patents.product_idea: A solar cold room at village markets where farmers pay a small fee per crate per day to keep vegetables and fruit fresh.
patents.who_it_helps: Small farmers who lose a large share of produce to spoilage and must sell fast at low prices.
patents.build_cost: Expensive: ₹5–10 lakh per room. Better started as a business plan with a partner or grant.
patents.risks: High capital cost; similar models exist (e.g. Ecozen, ColdHubs). Needs local operators.

patents.title: Hands-free urine collector for bedridden people at home
patents.original_title: Portable system for the collection of urine
patents.original_idea: A portable suction-based system that collects, deodorises and stores urine for people who cannot reach a toilet.
patents.why_it_stalled: Required a mains-powered motor/fan and was bulky and pricey, so it stayed in hospitals.
patents.what_changed: Small brushless fans and rechargeable batteries are cheap; better skin-safe materials exist.
patents.product_idea: A low-cost battery-powered urine collection system for bedridden elderly and disabled people in small homes, reducing bedsores and caregiver burden.
patents.who_it_helps: Elderly and disabled people cared for at home by family members, often women.
patents.risks: Comfort and hygiene need careful testing; competing imported products are expensive.

patents.title: LED micro-farm for urban women's self-help groups
patents.original_title: Method and apparatus for irradiation of plants using optoelectronic devices
patents.original_idea: Growing plants under arrays of LEDs in specific colours instead of sunlight.
patents.why_it_stalled: LEDs were dim and very expensive in 1988.
patents.what_changed: LED grow lights are now cheap and efficient.
patents.product_idea: A shelf-sized LED microgreens farm kit plus training, so self-help groups can sell fresh microgreens to city restaurants.
patents.who_it_helps: Low-income urban women seeking home-based income.
patents.risks: Microgreens is a niche market; needs nearby buyers; electricity costs.

patents.title: Gel-coated seeds that survive dry spells
patents.original_title: Method of applying gel coating to plant seeds
patents.original_idea: Wrapping each seed in a water-holding gel capsule with an air bubble.
patents.why_it_stalled: The coating machinery was industrial and expensive; small farmers had no access.
patents.what_changed: Seaweed-based gels (alginate) are cheap and simple coating equipment can be built locally.
patents.product_idea: A seed-coating service for direct-seeded rice and millets, helping seeds survive irregular monsoon rain.
patents.who_it_helps: Rain-fed farmers facing more erratic rainfall.
patents.risks: Needs field trials and agronomy partners; benefit varies by crop and soil.

patents.title: Solar air-to-water generator for humid coastal villages
patents.original_title: Portable, potable water recovery and dispensing apparatus
patents.original_idea: Making drinking water by cooling air until moisture condenses, then filtering and sterilising it.
patents.why_it_stalled: It uses a lot of electricity per litre, which was expensive and required grid power.
patents.what_changed: Solar power is much cheaper and compressors are more efficient, but the energy use per litre is still significant.
patents.product_idea: A solar water kiosk in humid coastal areas where groundwater is salty, selling drinking water by the can.
patents.who_it_helps: Coastal communities in Odisha, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Andhra with saline groundwater.
patents.risks: Works poorly in dry weather; water cost per litre may be higher than RO or delivered water. Existing companies sell such machines.

patents.title: Fold-out container shelter for floods and disasters
patents.original_idea: A shipping container whose side walls fold down to triple the floor space, with a fabric cover.
patents.why_it_stalled: Used mainly for industrial camps; costs were high and nothing powered it off-grid.
patents.what_changed: Used containers are cheap; solar roofs, LED lighting and water tanks can be built in.
patents.product_idea: A ready-to-deploy flood/cyclone relief shelter with solar power and water storage that state disaster authorities or NGOs can stockpile.
patents.who_it_helps: Families displaced by floods and cyclones (Assam, Odisha, Bihar).
patents.risks: Sales are to governments/NGOs (slow tenders). Heat inside steel containers needs insulation.

patents.title: Thin insulation panels for tin-roof homes in heatwaves
patents.original_idea: Very thin vacuum insulation panels held apart by glass beads.
patents.why_it_stalled: Vacuum panels were costly to make and fragile.
patents.what_changed: Still expensive, but heatwaves are worsening and cheaper alternatives (reflective coatings, foam-board) can deliver part of the benefit.
patents.product_idea: A cheap roof-insulation retrofit for metal-roofed slum homes; vacuum panels may be too costly, so start with a simpler insulated reflective panel.
patents.who_it_helps: Families in metal-roofed homes where indoor temperatures can exceed 45 °C.
patents.risks: Vacuum panels are probably too expensive for this market; the original idea mostly inspires rather than transfers directly.

patents.title: Solar panel that also makes hot water for clinics and hostels
patents.original_title: Solar concentrator for heat and electricity
patents.original_idea: A self-steering mirror concentrates sunlight on solar cells that are cooled by water, giving both electricity and hot water.
patents.why_it_stalled: Tracking mirrors and solar cells were expensive and complex.
patents.what_changed: Solar cells are cheap now; simple flat "PVT" panels give hot water and power without mirrors.
patents.product_idea: A combined solar panel + water heater for rural clinics, hostels and small hotels that need hot water.
patents.who_it_helps: Patients and students in rural institutions; saves firewood or electric heating.
patents.risks: Competes with cheap separate solar water heaters + panels; harder to sell the advantage.
